title: Approval Consumption Fix Live Verification
summary: After the operator restarted and refreshed the MCP service, runtime diagnostics showed the service PID changed from 787440 to 789985, activating the FP-MCP-234 bridge fix. Live validation again proved the FP-MCP-233 approval is expired and unusable and the old popup-created clearance is expired, stale against current HEAD, and ineligible. A post-restart consumption-recorder probe did not write consumption because the approval is expired, but it no longer emitted APPROVAL_SCOPE_MISMATCH, APPROVAL_REQUEST_BINDING_INVALID, or APPROVAL_TEXT_INVALID. This verifies the hardcoded FP-MCP-036 scope bug is no longer active in the live service. Retroactive consumption of the expired FP-MCP-233 approval remains impossible; future fresh successful starts must verify immediate approval consumption under the fixed recorder.
caveats: This does not retroactively consume the FP-MCP-233 approval.
The FP-MCP-233 approval remains unconsumed but expired and unusable.
The old local clearance remains present on disk but is expired and stale against current HEAD, therefore ineligible.

This verification proves the scope-mismatch bug is no longer active in the live service, but a future fresh unexpired approval path must still prove that consumption can be recorded immediately after a successful start.
No runner start, OpenCode start, or new execution occurred during this verification.
